1.overview: The LORD declares his love for Israel by contrasting Jacob with Esau and describing Edom’s lasting desolation. He rebukes Israel’s priests for dishonoring him with defective offerings, rejects their sacrifices, and declares that his name will be great among the nations.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Name Among the Nations

2.overview: The LORD threatens the priests with curses for dishonoring his name, recalls the covenant of life and peace with Levi, and condemns their corrupt teaching and partiality. Judah is accused of profaning the sanctuary through foreign marriages and of breaking faith with wives, while the people weary the LORD by calling evildoers good and questioning his justice.

sections.heading: The Priests and the Covenant of Levi

3.overview: The LORD announces a messenger who prepares the way, followed by the Lord’s coming to the temple to refine the Levites, restore acceptable offerings, and judge wrongdoing. He calls Jacob’s descendants to return, condemns their withholding of tithes, answers their complaints about serving God, and promises to distinguish and spare those who fear and honor him.

sections.heading: Return to the LORD and Bring Tithes
The Faithful and the Wicked Distinguished

4.overview: The LORD announces a coming day that consumes the arrogant and evildoers, while those who fear his name receive healing and trample the wicked. He calls Israel to remember the law given through Moses at Horeb and promises to send Elijah before the Day of the LORD to turn the hearts of parents and children, or bring a curse on the land.

sections.heading: Judgment and healing on the coming day
Moses, Elijah, and the Day of the LORD
